issues.body: The round-4 blocker remains materially unchanged: Store.validateStore and InitOutput.store_validateStore are added to the generated declaration file, but this diff contains no corresponding Rust/wasm implementation or generated JavaScript binding. TypeScript consumers can compile against validateStore and then encounter a missing method/export at runtime. Generated wasm-bindgen declarations must match the runtime artifacts.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the validateStore documentation, method declaration, cross-link, and InitOutput export from this PR. If the API is intended, implement it in the wasm source, add focused stateful/default-graph equivalence tests, update the matching public JS/WASM skill, and regenerate all wasm-bindgen artifacts instead of editing only the declaration file.
issues.title: Generated typings still declare validateStore without a runtime implementation

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant: the same major blocking issue from round 4 remains. The diff still adds Store.validateStore and store_validateStore only to the generated TypeScript declaration file, without corresponding Rust/wasm implementation or generated JavaScript glue in the diff. This advertises a callable API and low-level export that will be absent at runtime. The file-ingest picker refactor and focused tests appear coherent, but they do not resolve the false generated wasm API surface.
